recipes.title: Wine oxtail
recipes.description: 番茄紅酒炆牛尾 - tomato red wine braised oxtail. Serves 4-6.
steps: Sear the oxtail: heat a wide pan over medium-high and lightly sear the oxtail until the surface browns (no need to cook through); remove and set aside.

Sauté onions and shallots using the fat left from searing (add a little olive oil if needed): add the diced onions and cook until fragrant, then add the sliced shallots. Don't wash the pan - the browned bits add flavor.
When the onions turn translucent, add the diced carrots and celery; stir and cook until combined.
Add the tomato paste and sauté briefly until fragrant.
Turn off the heat and transfer everything to a large stew pot.
Over high heat, add the tomato purée and peeled canned tomatoes, mix well, then pour in the entire bottle of red wine.
Add the rosemary, thyme, and black pepper, and mix.

Add the seared oxtail. Braise on medium-low 45 minutes. Turn off the heat, cover, and rest 1 hour (residual heat gently softens the meat). Then simmer on medium-low another 30 minutes. Add a bit more rosemary and thyme if desired.
When the meat starts to fall off the bone it's done. Serve the same day, or cool and refrigerate - the flavor deepens overnight.

recipes.title: Bo Lu luc
recipes.description: Bò Lúc Lác - Vietnamese shaking beef with top sirloin.
ingredients: 1 lb top sirloin, cut into 1-inch cubes
Tenderizer: 1/2 tsp baking soda + 1-2 tbsp water
Dip: lime juice (1/2-1 lime) + pinch salt + lots of black pepper
steps: Tenderize (15-20 min): toss the beef with baking soda and a splash of water, wait 15-20 minutes, then rinse and pat VERY dry (important).
Marinate (10-30 min): toss the beef with the marinade and let it sit; if it looks wet, pat dry again.

Sear: heat the pan HIGH until smoking, add 1 tbsp oil, and add the beef in a single layer (2 batches if crowded). Don't move it for 45-60 sec, flip for 45 sec, quick toss 10-20 sec, then remove; repeat.
Finish (10-30 sec): lower to medium-high, add butter (and onion if using), toss the onion 30-45 sec, add the beef back, and toss 10-15 sec to glaze; off heat.
Serve with the lime-salt-pepper dip.

recipes.title: Cold sear
steps: Pull at 90°F, rest 10 min → medium-well, finishes at 123°F.
Pull at 75°F, rest 10 min → medium-rare, finishes at 110°F.
Try 70°F next time for more rare.

recipes.title: Reverse sear
recipes.description: Reverse-sear temperature log for various cuts.
steps: Oven at 220°F, using a thermometer.
Tenderloin: pull at 95°F and rest (2.5-inch steak). 100°F was too cooked, 90°F a bit too raw, 96°F almost good (a tad over) - try 93°F next time.
Ribeye: pull at 105°F (120°F is too cooked), 2.5-inch steak. Latest: pull at 105°F, finish to 110°F manually. Miso marinade needs 4+ hours.
Tomahawk (thick): pull at 107°F, rest 10, rest until 110°F for rare. Update 8/24/2026 - a 107°F pull was a disaster (too much juice lost); try pulling at 100°F next time.

recipes.title: Satay beef noodle
recipes.description: 沙嗲牛肉麵 - satay beef noodles. Notes: keeps 4+ days; V2 was too salty overnight so soy sauce was cut from 1 tbsp to 1/2; baking powder reduced from 3 to 2 tsp to cut the powdery taste; Skippy is sweeter/more peanutty and Jif less so, so half-and-half is preferred; 2/18 - try 1 tbsp baking powder per 1 lb beef next time.
ingredients: 牛冧肉 / Beef, 300g (thinly sliced across the grain, soaked to remove blood)
Marinade: white pepper / oyster sauce 1/2 tsp
Marinade: Shaoxing wine / dark soy sauce 1/2 tsp each
Satay sauce: sacha sauce (沙茶醬), 3 tbsp
Satay sauce: peanut butter, 2 tbsp (best is half Skippy no-peanut + half Jif with peanut, i.e. 1 tbsp each)
steps: Marinate the beef overnight (best) or at least 4 hours.
Make the satay sauce: mix the sacha sauce, peanut butter, sugar, and water.
Heat a wok on high with a little oil and stir-fry the beef to 60-70% done; set aside.
Add a little oil, sauté the garlic until fragrant, then add the satay sauce (2-3 min on medium heat).
Add the beef back and cook until thickened (~2 min); set aside.
Boil water, cook the instant noodles, drain, top with the satay beef, and finish with sesame oil.
Tip: add 1 tsp chicken powder and a little noodle water (about half the cooking water), then add the noodles and top with the satay beef.

recipes.title: Thai style ribeye
recipes.description: Crying Tiger Steak Sandwich (from owen.han) - Thai-style ribeye. Only the ingredient list was saved from the original.
steps: Note: only the ingredient list was saved from the original (owen.han). Build it as a steak sandwich - season/sear the ribeye with fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce and brown sugar, spread the compound butter (butter + brown sugar + fish sauce + chili flakes + cilantro + lime) on sourdough, and top with the sliced chili, red onion, cilantro, and crispy garlic chips.

recipes.title: 煲仔沙嗲牛肉麵
recipes.description: 煲仔沙嗲牛肉麵 - claypot satay beef noodles. One serving.
ingredients: Beef marinade: light soy sauce 1 tsp, dark soy sauce 1 tsp, rice wine 1 tsp, white pepper 1/2 tsp, cornstarch 1 tsp, water 1 tbsp, oil 1 tbsp
Satay sauce: satay sauce (沙嗲醬) 2 tbsp, sacha sauce (沙茶醬) 1/2 tbsp, coarse peanut butter 1.5 tbsp, shrimp paste 1/2 tsp
Satay seasoning: light soy sauce 1 tbsp, dark soy sauce 1 tbsp, oyster sauce 1/2 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp
steps: Slice the beef, add the marinade, and marinate 15 minutes.
Stir-fry the beef until about 80-90% cooked; set aside.
Mix the satay sauce (satay sauce, sacha sauce, peanut butter, shrimp paste) with the seasoning.
Sauté the minced garlic and shallot until fragrant, add the satay sauce and stir-fry, then add ~350ml water and bring the sauce to a boil; set aside.
Heat a claypot, add the enoki, tofu puffs, satay sauce, instant noodles, and ~50ml water; cover and cook 3 minutes.
After 3 minutes, add the cooked beef, cover, and cook another 2 minutes.
